title: Low-Pass Filter - Band 25 (1900 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Lena Kowalski

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Low-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 25 (1900 MHz) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on ScAlN on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 1892.8 MHz and bandwidth of 262.2 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Low-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 25 (1900 MHz)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: ScAlN on Si
- Package: WLP (Wafer Level Package)
- Design Tool: COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2
- Design Center: Osaka Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Low-Pass Filter design targeting Band 25 (1900 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1892.8 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       262.2 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.1 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 21.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 39.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 27.0 dB
Q Factor:               7090
Temperature Coefficient:-8.2 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.9 x 2.0 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   5
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 and load the Low-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: ScAlN on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1892.8 MHz, BW 262.2 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.1 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (WLP (Wafer Level Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, ScAlN on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N9041B UXA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 5678 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.1 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 21.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 393 MHz offset >= 39.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 2 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 1.9 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +25 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 93%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-11-13
Devices Tested:         73
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.82 dB
Return Loss (meas):     23.1 dB
Rejection (meas):       42.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       32.4 dB
Q Factor (meas):        7090
Group Delay Variation:  2.8 ns
Power Handling:         +28 dBm
Die Yield:              88.5%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Low-Pass Filter design demonstrated acceptable performance for Band 25 (1900 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Group delay flatness improved compared to previous revision.
e) ESD robustness exceeded specification by 2x margin.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
